newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Lufthansa warns Boeing on future procurement.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Lufthansa warns Boeing on future procurement.

text.p: German airline Lufthansa AG warned on Thursday that its future procurement of aircraft from Boeing Co could be affected by the U.S. group's plans to enter airline maintenance.
A Lufthansa spokesman confirmed comments by chairman Juergen Weber in the German business daily "Handelsblatt" describing any such a move by Boeing as "bad business behaviour".
Lufthansa, which has sourced around half of its fleet from Boeing, is also a world leader in jet maintenance, particularly outside the United States.
"If Boeing sets up in competition to us, it will have an impact on our future procurement. After all, we don't build airplanes," Weber was quoted as telling journalists in New York.
The Lufthansa spokesman confirmed that a reduction in future purchases from the U.S. plane-maker was a possible outcome of Boeing's decision to enter aircraft maintenance.
Boeing confirmed earlier this month that it was considering taking over maintenance operations for some of its airline customers as part of a diversification drive.
Media reports have listed British Airways Plc as one possible client, although neither Boeing nor the British airline have commented on the speculation.

Lufthansa Technik, Lufthansa's maintenance division, contributed third quarter pre-tax profits of 44 million marks ($25.6 million), around a tenth of the group total. Sales for the quarter stood at 2.1 billion marks, with 852 million marks of that coming outside of the group.

The division, which has operations in Hamburg and Ireland, employs just over 10,000 staff, around a sixth of the group total. It expects profits to rise for the 1996 year as a whole despite increasing international competition.

Weber also hit out at "exclusive provider" relationships recently forged between Boeing and airlines such as AMR Corp's American Airlines and Delta, saying that Lufthansa would never enter such an arrangement.
"We shall continue to buy the best airplanes at the most favourable prices," he was quoted as saying.
